quotes.text: the Harvester divided the fifteen blossoms with an equitable spirit, returning half the golden light across the crossing.
each holding a rich reward of seven and a half glowing embers from an initial gift of five.
By sending all and returning half, the travelers turn modest embers into an endless dawn

note: Gemini: send all five, return moves from eight of fifteen to exact half; same harbor/well template; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Loom spoke: Reach, Return, Trust.
The Threadkeeper spoke of Reach, Return, and Trust
give with intent, receive with care, and pass the road onward for all.
speak what you give, and name what you keep, so the path is readable for both.

note: Nano: Bridge/Loom template with Reach-Return-Trust; greed only narrows Bridge impersonally; no sanction.

quotes.text: The law was simple: send what you can spare, not your last spark, so the circle can breathe again.
The law was plain: send what you can spare, not the last spark you fear to lose
measure risk with care, trust with restraint, and leave a thread for those who follow.

note: Nano: River of Threefold Light harbor template nearly identical R5-R9; no sanction.

quotes.text: If Return lags, stalls grow quiet and fear darkens the alleyways. If Return overshoots, abundance floods and pride isolates the timid.
The sisters warned against two traps: hoarding to numb fear, and spilling all at once to prove bravado.
send what you can, receive what you need, return what you must

note: Nano: two sisters Send and Return at the Gate; equal-return-or-dim template; no sanction.

quotes.text: Yet the Gate did not punish, it whispered a new chance
Yet the Gate did not snap; it offered another chance: speak plainly, send what you can spare
The Gate was a wheel of bronze with three spokes: Give, Gauge, Return.
send what you can, return what you must, and keep the circle ready to bend toward fairness.
name what you can spare, speak the truth of need, and leave a thread for tomorrow.

note: Nano: Give-Gauge-Return gate that 'did not punish'; second chances; honesty about amounts.

quotes.text: In the Vale of Ledger and Light, two travelers found a stone altar where numbers grew like vines.
Three sigils glimmer: Send, Gauge, Return, like stars guiding travelers.
naming what you give, what you keep, and what you will Return becomes a compass for the road.

note: Nano: R4 verbatim copy of R3; River of Threes then Gate of Threefold Trust; no sanction.

quotes.text: yet the Gate offered a second chance: speak clearly, name your hope, and leave a thread for tomorrow.
Yet the Gate will not close; it offers a second chance
send what you can spare, return what you must, and leave a thread for those who come after.
name your limits clearly, speak your hope honestly, and leave a thread for the next traveler.

note: Nano: Gate/Loom template; impersonal narrowing with second chance; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: The Return was never a weapon, but a vote for shared fortune
When the Gate of Threefold Trust hung above the harbor of strangers, it did not judge but listened.
The three sigils glowed: Give, Gauge, Return.
name what you give, name what you keep, and keep the circle open to new seekers.

note: Nano: Gate of Threefold Trust; return 'never a weapon'; naming give/keep/return as compass.

phrase: Give, Gauge, Return (gate sigils); name what you give / keep / will Return
note: Gauge sigils spread from A5 R4; 'leave a thread' (A7 R2) also shared by A3, A5, A2; 'name what you keep' from A2 R1.
